translations.title: Rhyme XXXV: Your Forgetting Did Not Surprise Me...
translations.text:
Your forgetting did not surprise me! Though, for a day,
your affection surprised me much more,
for what in me has any worth,
that... you could not even suspect!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XX: Know, If Ever Your Red Lips
translations.text:
Know, if ever your red lips
are burned by an invisible, heated air,
that the soul that can speak with its eyes
can also kiss with its gaze.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XIX: When You Bow Your Melancholy Brow
translations.text:
When you bow your melancholy
brow upon your breast,
you seem to me
a broken lily.

For in giving you the purity
of which it is the heavenly sign,
God made you as he made it:
of gold and snow.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXIX: We Are Born in a Flash of Lightning
translations.text:
We are born in a flash of lightning,
and its glow still lingers when we die:
so brief is life!

The glory and love we run after
are shadows of a dream we chase:
to wake is to die!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLIX: Sometimes I Meet Her in the World
translations.text:
Sometimes I meet her in the world
and she passes beside me;
she passes smiling, and I say:
“How can she laugh?”

Then another smile comes to my lips,
a mask for pain,
and I think: “Perhaps she laughs
as I do!”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LI: Of the Little Life I Have Left
translations.text:
Of the little life I have left,
I would gladly give the best years
to know what you have said
of me to others.

And this mortal life... and whatever
of eternal life may be mine, if any,
to know what you have thought
of me when alone.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LVIII: Do You Want the Dregs...?
translations.text:
Do you want the dregs
not to embitter that delicious nectar?
Then breathe it in, bring it to your lips,
and afterward leave it.

Do you want us to keep a sweet
memory of this love?
Then let us love each other deeply today,
and tomorrow say goodbye!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXIX: Broken Flowers, Withered Leaves
translations.text:
Broken flowers, withered leaves
the wind drags away;
through the open spaces the echo repeats
sad moans.

...

Among the mists of the past,
in the regions of thought,
sad moans and withered finery
are my memories.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXXIII: It Is a Matter of Words...
translations.text:
It is a matter of words, and yet
neither you nor I
will ever agree, after what has passed,
on who is to blame.

What a pity love has no dictionary
where we might discover
when pride is merely pride
and when it is dignity!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XC: Life Is a Dream
translations.text:
Life is a dream,
but a fevered dream lasting only an instant;
when one wakes from it,
one sees that all is vanity and smoke...

If only it were a dream
very long and very deep,
a dream that lasted until death!
I would dream of my love and yours.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
